sources.title: v0: User interface
sources.finding: v0 provides a browser chat, tool cards, live previews and browser-use screenshots.

sources.title: v0: Invoking an agent; Unsupported configurations
sources.finding: The v0 sandbox includes a supported Claude Code wrapper invoked with claude. Traffic uses Vercel AI Gateway; direct binaries, rerouting with personal API keys and added unvetted agents are outside the supported configuration.

sources.title: v0: How do credits work; Using a ChatGPT subscription
sources.locator: How do credits work; Using a ChatGPT subscription
sources.finding: v0 credits pay for generation and platform fees. Eligible OpenAI responses can use a linked ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan, while image work, delegated subagents and other supporting work still consume v0 credits. This is not a coding-agent native subscription login.

sources.title: v0: Import an existing repository
sources.finding: A GitHub import creates a chat on a selected base branch; the first generated change creates a working branch and hosted preview.

sources.title: v0: Overview
sources.finding: The v0 API creates chats and apps, sends messages, embeds authenticated previews and deploys to Vercel. The SDK includes React and AI SDK integrations, and an MCP server is documented.

sources.title: v0: MCP integrations
sources.finding: Users can connect preset or custom MCP servers to give v0 additional external tools during generation.

sources.title: v0: How it works
sources.finding: The beta Slack bot accepts @v0 prompts, reads the thread and creates a code branch and pull request. Continuing the same thread continues the chat and branch.

sources.title: v0: Built-in presets
sources.finding: The Plan Mode instruction asks v0 to outline an approach, steps and risks and request approval before implementing. This is a reusable instruction preset, not verified enforced policy.

sources.title: v0: Creating custom instructions; Applying instructions
sources.finding: Reusable named instructions are saved to the account, available across chats and projects and applied until unchecked.

sources.title: v0: Web search; Browser use
sources.finding: v0 searches the web with linked sources and uses a browser to inspect previews or external sites, supplying screenshots in chat.

sources.title: v0: Agent control
sources.finding: Users can stop the agent, see tool execution cards and follow automatic continuation through multi-step work.

sources.title: v0: Getting started
sources.finding: Natural-language requests select web search, browser use, integrations or terminal execution; action progress is visible in chat.

sources.title: v0: What the sandbox is
sources.finding: VM-backed chats run project files, Node.js preview servers and shell commands in Vercel Sandbox virtual machines.

sources.title: v0: June 26, 2026 fixes
sources.finding: The changelog states that preview sandboxes no longer time out during long generations, including when the tab is closed.

sources.title: v0: Isolation boundaries
sources.finding: Each VM-backed chat has separate files, processes and environment variables; sandbox ownership follows the chat owner and shared-chat access. Production uses separate infrastructure. Outbound network policy defaults to allow-all and is configurable by team owners.

sources.title: v0: Lifecycle
sources.finding: The chat filesystem persists between sessions. A pool sandbox begins at thirty minutes and active sandboxes extend by ten minutes near expiry, up to twenty-four hours. Expired sandboxes are recreated on a later action.

sources.title: v0: What runs inside
sources.finding: Sandboxes include Node.js and pnpm, npm, yarn and bun; a framework-aware dev server starts on the appropriate port with linked Vercel environment variables.

sources.title: v0: Lifecycle
sources.finding: A sandbox has an absolute twenty-four-hour maximum and receives automatic active-use extensions within that cap. This is not a guarantee of multi-day process survival.

sources.title: v0: Real-time feedback
sources.finding: Chat shows progress indicators, tool execution cards, browser screenshots and source links; deployment Fix with v0 sends error logs back to the agent.

sources.title: v0: Usage and billing
sources.finding: The dashboard groups credit consumption by chat or project. Team Owners and Billing roles can inspect member and project usage. Model costs are available in the selector.

sources.title: v0: Sharing Chats; Inviting team members
sources.finding: Team members can receive Can Edit access to a chat and generate changes; shared chat history is included on Plus, Business and Enterprise. Simultaneous input ordering was not tested.

sources.title: v0: Team access; Enterprise
sources.finding: Plus members have Builder access. Enterprise adds Builder, Creator and Viewer roles, free viewer seats, SAML SSO and audit logs. Vercel Owners have direct administrative read access to team-owned chats.

sources.title: v0: Terminal commands
sources.finding: Sandbox terminal execution has Ask, Auto and Full permission modes; actual deny and revoke enforcement was not tested.

sources.title: v0: Edit code
sources.finding: Save commits tracked manual file changes and Discard restores the latest commit; generated message versions retain a read-only Diff tab.

sources.title: v0: Review changes
sources.finding: A message Diff tab displays version changes; users can select diff lines and attach comments to the next prompt.

sources.title: v0: Transferring chats and projects
sources.finding: Chats can be transferred between personal and team scopes, bringing the full prior history into the team-owned chat. This is not a verified live human takeover.

sources.title: v0: Browser use; User interface
sources.finding: Browser-use screenshots and preview context appear in chat along with tool output.

sources.title: v0: Branch protection and blocked publishes
sources.finding: The GitHub Publish flow respects required checks, reviews, draft state and branch protections; blocked merges remain open with links and an explanation. This enforcement is documented rather than observed.

sources.title: v0: How v0 works with Git; Branch menu
sources.locator: How v0 works with Git; Branch menu
sources.finding: v0 automatically commits and pushes to a chat working branch, creates PRs, displays CI and offers fixes for CI or conflicts. Separate chats can share a repository with distinct branches.

sources.title: v0: Publish GitHub changes
sources.finding: Publish creates or reuses a pull request, merges to its base branch and waits for production deployment, subject to branch protection. v0 roles do not grant deployment permissions in GitHub or Vercel CLI.

sources.title: v0: Versions
sources.finding: Users can view and restore previous generated versions. No stale-approval invalidation scenario was exercised.

sources.title: v0: Browse files
sources.finding: The code viewer can copy or download files, including pending edits. This does not establish export of the entire ADE or portable chat/task history.

sources.title: v0: Data privacy and training
sources.finding: Enterprise customers can opt out of having their content used for model training, and Enterprise data is processed on separate infrastructure. The page does not separate Vercel and model-provider data policies. This is not a telemetry disable control.

sources.title: v0: Plan comparison; Free credits
sources.finding: Plus costs USD 30 per user monthly and Business USD 100, with USD 30 monthly credits each. Legacy Premium is USD 20 monthly but closed to new users. New Free signups receive a one-time USD 5 offer, while existing Free users retain USD 5 monthly.
